To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sulfamidase is an important enzyme for the metabolism of heparan sulfate, that it is deficient in the Sanfilippo type I syndrome, that the enzyme can be assayed in cultured skin fibroblast and that it can be assayed with a tetrasaccharidic substrate.

sulfamidase, a lysosomal hydrolase that catalyses the hydrolysis of GlcNS-UOAs to GlcNS-Ids, has been purified to homogeneity, and the cDNA has been cloned, sequenced and expressed in Escherichia coli.

the use of a radiolabelted tetrasaccharides as substrate in the assay of the enzyme activity of the sulfamidase in cultured human fibroblasts, allows a clear and reliable distinction to be made between Sanfilippo type-A patients and normal controls, and between Sanfilippo A and other mucopolisacharidosis types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new substrate for sulfamidases.
the development of a rapid and sensitive assay for the diagnosis of Sanfilippo A disease.
the development of a rapid and simple method for the diagnosis of the Sanfilipo A syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sulfamidase is a lysosomal enzyme which hydrolyses a tetrasaccharidic substrate containing GlcNS-UOAs, GlcNS-UA and GlcNS.
sulfamidase can be detected in normal fibroblasts using the tetrasaccheride, trisacharide and disacchardie substrates but not in fibroblasts from Sanfilippo patients.
the radiolabelled GlcNS-UA- GlcNS-UOAsulfamidase assay is the most sensitive and reliable method for the diagnosis of the Sanfilppo A syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tetrasaccheride substrate is the most appropriate substrate for the routine enzymological diagnosis of the Sanfilipo A syndrome.
the tetrasaccheride GlcNS-UA-D-[6, 2H]idonic Acid, GlcNS-UA-L-[6,3H]guluronic acid and GluNS-UA-L-[3H]iduronic Acid was the most sensitive and specific substrate for the detection of Sanfilippo A.

GlcNS-UA-D-glucosamininitol-N-sulfate is a very useful substrate for the diagnosis of Sanfilippo B syndrome and GlcNS-UA-(GlcNAcUA)-D-glucosaminitol-N-sulfate (the tetrasaccharidic substrate) for the diagnosis of the Sanfilppo A syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tetrasacchride substrate is more sensitive for detecting Sanfilippo A.
the use of the tetrasaccheride substrate for sulfamidases is a more sensitive assay for the diagnosis of Sanfilippo syndrome type A than other substrates.
we have identified a substrate that is highly specific for the enzyme and that is not found in any other MPS type.
